# external.targeted_signal

## Purpose
Row-level record of DDP (Data Deal Partner) signals that were actually **used for targeting** — the
decomposition the monthly meter (`coredw.usage_reporting_data`) hides. Reach for it to answer "which
vendor (`source_data_source_id`) contributed which signal (`data_source_category_id`) on which IP on a
given day," to reconstruct DDP vendor crediting / first-reporter analysis, and to audit MM
(site-visit / keyword) usage that the meter reports only as NULL-`data_source_category_id` aggregate
rows. It is a BQ **external table** over Parquet in `gs://mntn-data-archive-prod/signals/targeted_signal/`.

## Grain & keys
- **Grain:** one row per **used signal event** — `uid` × `ip` × `data_source_category_id`, nested under
  the hive partitions `data_source_id` × `dt` × `source_data_source_id`. An IP appears on many rows (one
  per dsc_id it matched, ordinal in `ip_to_dscid_link_number`).
- **Natural key:** (`data_source_id`, `dt`, `source_data_source_id`, `uid`, `data_source_category_id`).
- **Join / foreign columns:** `data_source_category_id` → `bronze.tpa.categories.data_source_category_id`
  (segment / keyword decode); `source_data_source_id` → the crediting DDP vendor (see `ds_catalog.md`);
  `ip` → impression/log IPs (no IP→IP bridging in BQ — join on exact string).

## Column meanings (only the non-obvious ones)
- `uid` — ULID of the underlying signal/site-visit event (e.g. `01KXX49MW1CZKA2MCY3YGQSC4P`); the dedup +
  lineage key back to the source site-visit-signal (svs) row.
- `ip` — the household/device IP the signal was matched to (string; join by exact match, no bridging).
- `data_source_category_id` (dsc_id) — the segment / keyword the signal counts toward. For MM keyword
  (DS19) this is a keyword ID from the ~20k targetable-keyword universe; for MM site-visit (DS13) a
  category ID. Decode via `bronze.tpa.categories`. In `usage_reporting_data` this column is NULL for MM
  vendors — this table is where the DS13-vs-DS19 / per-category decomposition actually lives.
- `source_time` — TIMESTAMP the signal actually fired at the source (the real event time; typically 1–2
  days before `dt`).
- `time` — TIMESTAMP the row was stamped into the partition — observed as the **end-of-day marker**
  (`<dt> 23:59:59`), not the true event time. Use `source_time` for real timing, not `time`.
- `signal_type_id` — INT signal-type enum (all sampled rows = 1). Full enum not yet decoded.
- `ip_to_dscid_link_number` — ordinal (1,2,3…) of this IP→dsc_id link within the partition; an IP that
  matched multiple categories gets one row per category, numbered.
- `data_source_id` (hive) — the DDP *pathway*, not the vendor: **4 = CRM, 13 = MM site-visit, 19 = MM
  keyword** (the three top-level prefixes present in GCS).
- `dt` (hive) — STRING date `YYYY-MM-DD`, the reporting day. This is the effective time partition.
- `source_data_source_id` (hive) — the **credited DDP vendor** that supplied the signal (e.g. 23/24/25/
  26/28/30/33/36…); resolve vendor names via `ds_catalog.md`. This is the "who gets paid" dimension the
  meter collapses away.

## Joins & relationships
- **Upstream:** a subset of site-visit-signal (svs) where a `dsc_id` is derivable (via
  `product_categorization`); svs→targeted_signal is **1:many** (one svs event fans out to one row per
  matched category).
- **Downstream billing chain:** targeted_signal (used rows) → `prod.mntn_matched.mntn_matched_reporting`
  (Athena) → `coredw.usage_reporting_data` (BQ, month-end snapshots) → monthly vendor payout.
- **Fan-out warning:** joining on `ip` alone multiplies — an IP carries many dsc_id rows across many
  vendors per day. Deduplicate to your grain (e.g. DISTINCT `ip` or `ip`+`source_data_source_id`) before
  counting. Rows are **raw used-signal events, NOT billed impressions** — do not sum rows as if they were
  impressions or dollars; billing still needs the first-reporter / credit-split rule applied downstream.

## Gotchas
- **`numRows`/`numBytes` = 0** in `bq show` — it is an external table; BQ has no row/byte stats. Size is
  inferred from the underlying Parquet (one DS13 × 1 day × 1 vendor leaf ≈ 46.7k rows).
- **Not a view over sqlmesh** — `physical_table: self`; source is GCS Parquet, not a `sqlmesh__*` table.
- **`time` is an end-of-day sentinel** (`23:59:59`), not the event time — use `source_time`.
- **Meter mismatch is expected:** `usage_reporting_data.data_source_category_id` is NULL for MM vendors;
  this table holds the decomposition the meter lacks. Row counts here ≠ billed impressions.
- **dt coverage:** production since ~2025-05-02 (DS19 backfilled from 2025-04-20); GCS shows continuous
  daily `dt=` partitions through the current day. Historical earliest partition ~mid-2025.
- **Credit-regime break:** downstream billing switched from fractional (Jan–Apr 2026) to integer
  single-vendor credit (May 2026+). This table is the raw used-signal input; the winner/split rule lives
  in dbt (`targeted_signal_ds_13/19`, DAG `keyword_ddp_reporting`), not in these columns.

## Cost & partitioning notes
- **Always filter the hive partitions** `dt` (STRING `YYYY-MM-DD`), `data_source_id` (4/13/19), and
  `source_data_source_id` (vendor). `require_partition_filter` is **not enforced** by BQ on this external
  table, so an unfiltered scan will read the entire GCS archive — filter defensively.
- **Partition-column-only aggregations bill $0** (metadata-served); scans that read `uid`/`ip`/`dsc_id`/
  `time` read the Parquet leaves. One leaf partition (1 DS × 1 day × 1 vendor) ≈ 46.7k rows / ~10 MB.
- No BQ clustering (external). No BQ TTL — retention is GCS-archive lifecycle on
  `gs://mntn-data-archive-prod/signals/targeted_signal/`.
- Avoid `SELECT *` across many days × vendors; prune to the specific `dt` / vendor / pathway you need.

## Example queries
```sql
-- Which vendors credited signals on an IP for one MM-site-visit day (partition-pruned)
SELECT source_data_source_id, COUNT(*) AS used_rows, COUNT(DISTINCT ip) AS ips
FROM `dw-main-bronze.external.targeted_signal`
WHERE data_source_id = 13
  AND dt = '2026-07-20'
GROUP BY source_data_source_id
ORDER BY used_rows DESC
```
